title: A Baby Garden
strapline: Grass under bare feet, herbs to crush, wind in the wind-chimes — the outdoors brought within a baby's reach.
intent: Bring babies outdoors into a garden made for their senses — soft grass, scented herbs, dappled light, gentle sound and safe things to touch.
Offer the qualities only outdoors can give: real weather on the skin, natural light, birdsong, the smell of earth after rain.
Support movement and exploration on varied natural surfaces — grass, bark, cool paving — for hands, knees and bare feet.
Build the earliest connection with the living world, the roots of caring for nature that grow through the years.
Keep it calm, close and unhurried, so a baby's first garden feels wonderful and safe.
implementation: Create a low, safe outdoor space: a patch of grass, planters of soft herbs, a willow arch, wind-chimes and ribbons, safe natural loose parts.
Let babies down onto the grass to sit, roll, crawl and feel the ground, with a blanket for those not yet mobile.
Brush herbs against little hands so the scent releases ('smell the mint — crush it in your fingers').
Follow what catches them — the moving shadows, the swaying grasses, the chime in the wind — and name it softly.
Check the space for hazards, keep planting non-toxic and mouth-safe, provide shade, and stay close throughout.
key_questions: What does the grass feel like under your feet?
Can you smell the herbs when we brush them?
Can you hear the chimes when the wind blows?
Shall we watch the leaves move in the breeze?

impact.text: Babies explore natural materials and surfaces outdoors with all their senses — grass, bark, herbs, light and sound.
A baby notices and delights in the outdoor world — the wind, the leaves, a passing bird, the swaying grass.
Babies respond with their whole bodies to the garden — bouncing to birdsong, reaching for a chime, patting the grass.
On grass, bark and paving a baby crawls, sits and pulls up, exploring freely on varied natural ground.

enhancements: Planters of soft, safe herbs — mint, lemon balm, lavender — at a baby's reaching height.
Wind-chimes, ribbons and streamers strung low to catch the breeze and the eye.
A willow arch or dappled shade for light and shadow to move through.
A natural treasure basket taken outdoors — pinecones, shells and stones under the open sky.
A shallow tray of rainwater or a puddle to pat, splash and watch.

playing_exploring: The baby explores the garden freely through every sense — touch, smell, sight and sound.
The outdoors offers real, changing sensations no indoor tray can match.
active_learning: Babies stay absorbed in the moving grass, dancing shadows and singing chimes for long, calm stretches.
creating_thinking: A baby links the wind to the chime and the ribbon's dance, beginning to expect the world to respond.
